name: IBM Design Language
owner: IBM Brand & Design (IBM Design Language) with Carbon Design System for digital product surfaces
design_principles: Good design is good business — design is a business discipline at IBM, not decoration
Carry the hierarchy with type and grid; color is a signal, never the structure
Neutral ground, deliberate accent — restraint is the brand's most recognizable trait
Every surface is accessible by default; accessibility is a requirement, not a review step
One system, many expressions — product, marketing, and event surfaces flex within the same grammar

identity.primary_mark: The IBM 8-bar logo — the striped 'IBM' wordmark designed by Paul Rand in 1972, still the sole primary mark.
mark_variants: Positive 8-bar mark in IBM Blue or black on light backgrounds
Reversed (white) 8-bar mark on dark or photographic backgrounds
Single-color monochrome mark where reproduction constraints require it
identity.lockup_rules: The 8-bar mark locks up with product and offering names as typographic sign-offs; sub-brands are set in IBM Plex alongside the mark rather than receiving marks of their own.
identity.clear_space: Clear space is derived from the mark's own bar height — nothing intrudes within that measure on any side.
identity.minimum_size: Reproduce no smaller than the size at which all eight bars remain individually legible.
misuse_rules: Never redraw, restripe, or regenerate the 8-bar mark — it is reproduced from approved artwork only
Never recolor the mark outside the approved positive, reversed, and monochrome variants
Never apply effects — shadows, gradients, outlines, bevels, or textures
Never place the mark on imagery busy enough to break the bars
Never stretch, rotate, or alter the proportions of the mark
identity.co_branding_rules: In partner and client lockups the IBM mark holds equal visual weight, separated by a clear rule, with the relationship stated in words rather than implied by scale.

palette.name: IBM Blue 60
palette.usage_notes: The brand's anchor blue and the primary interactive color across digital surfaces. Used deliberately, not as a background wash.

palette.name: Gray 100
palette.usage_notes: The canonical dark surface and the default text color on light backgrounds.

palette.name: White
palette.usage_notes: The default light surface. The system's neutral ground is the majority of any composition.

palette.name: Gray 10
palette.usage_notes: Layering and separation on light surfaces without introducing a border.

palette.name: Red 60
palette.usage_notes: Semantic only. Never used as a decorative or brand accent.

usage_rules: Neutrals carry the composition; blue is the accent that directs action
Semantic colors (error, success, warning) never do decorative work
Color never carries meaning alone — pair it with type, icon, or position
Gradients are used sparingly and only from the published gradient set
modes: Light themes (White, Gray 10) and dark themes (Gray 90, Gray 100) are both first-class; every component resolves in both
High-contrast requirements are met by the theme tokens, not by ad-hoc overrides

typefaces.name: IBM Plex Sans
typefaces.foundry: Commissioned by IBM (Mike Abbink with Bold Monday)
typefaces.license: Open source under the SIL Open Font License 1.1 — free for desktop, web, and embedding, which removes the seat-licensing constraint most brand systems carry

typefaces.name: IBM Plex Serif
typefaces.foundry: Commissioned by IBM (Mike Abbink with Bold Monday)

typefaces.name: IBM Plex Mono
typefaces.foundry: Commissioned by IBM (Mike Abbink with Bold Monday)

usage_rules: Type carries the hierarchy — set headings large and light rather than heavy and colored
Sentence case throughout; the system does not shout in all caps
Left-aligned by default; centered type is the exception, not a style choice
Never set body copy in the display size, and never set display copy in the body face's UI weights

imagery.art_direction: Photography documents real people doing real work and real technology in real environments. The point of view is observational and unstaged — the viewer is present in a working moment, not being sold at.
subject_matter: Practitioners and clients at work in their actual environments
Technology and infrastructure shown honestly at its own scale
Abstract and macro texture where a literal subject would mislead
imagery.treatment: Natural light, true color, minimal retouching. No heavy filters, no synthetic blue technology wash, no lens flare.
imagery.sourcing: Commissioned photography is preferred; stock is used only where it can pass as documentary. Imagery of clients requires their approval.
imagery.representation: Casting reflects the actual global workforce — a range of ages, geographies, abilities, and roles. Never symbolic diversity in an otherwise generic scene.
dos: Show the work, the tool, and the person in the same frame where possible
Leave compositional room for type — imagery and the grid are designed together
donts: No glowing blue circuit-board or 'digital brain' clichés
No composites that imply a product capability that does not exist

iconography.style: Geometric, consistent stroke weight, drawn on a fixed pixel grid, minimal detail. Icons read at their smallest intended size before any other consideration.
iconography.source: The Carbon icon library is the canonical set; new icons are contributed to it rather than drawn locally.
iconography.illustration_style: Flat, geometric, constructed from the same grid as the icons. Illustration explains a system or relationship; it does not decorate a page.
usage_rules: Use an existing Carbon icon before drawing a new one
Icons inherit text color; they are not independently colored for emphasis
An icon never carries meaning without an accessible label

principles: Motion explains cause and effect — where a thing came from and where it went
Productive motion gets out of the way; expressive motion is reserved for moments that deserve attention
motion.durations: Short, functional durations for productive UI transitions; longer, more deliberate durations for expressive brand moments.
motion.easing: Standard, entrance, and exit easing curves are defined as tokens; entrances decelerate and exits accelerate.
usage_rules: Honor reduced-motion preferences — the experience must be complete without motion
Motion never gates comprehension: nothing meaningful is visible only mid-animation

layout.grid: The 2x Grid — a 16-column responsive grid built on a 2x-based unit, with a visible relationship between the grid and the type scale.
layout.spacing_scale: A single token-based spacing scale derived from the 2x unit; no arbitrary spacing values.
composition_principles: Align to the grid and let the grid show — structure is part of the brand
Generous whitespace is a deliberate signal of confidence, not empty space to fill
One clear focal point per composition

accessibility.conformance_target: IBM Accessibility Requirements — aligned to WCAG 2.x Level AA, plus US Section 508 and EN 301 549
accessibility.contrast_requirements: Minimum 4.5:1 for body text and 3:1 for large text and meaningful non-text elements; theme tokens are built to satisfy this without manual checking.
accessibility.minimum_type_size: Body copy is never set below the body-01 step on any digital surface.
requirements: Every image carries meaningful alternative text; decorative images are explicitly marked as such
Color is never the only carrier of meaning
All interactive elements have a visible focus state and are fully keyboard operable
Video is captioned; audio content has a transcript

channel_specs.specifications: The 8-bar mark and a single typographic message; compositions are built for the smallest crop first and checked against each platform's safe zones before the widest.
Web-safe fallback stack assumed; layout holds at a single column, and no meaning depends on an image that may not load.
Large-format applications hold the 2x Grid and clear-space rules at scale; the mark is reproduced from vector artwork only.

brand_architecture_rules: IBM is a masterbrand — offerings are named and set typographically rather than given their own marks
Acquired brands transition to the IBM masterbrand on a defined timeline rather than persisting as visual peers
Open-source projects IBM stewards may hold their own community identity while carrying an IBM endorsement line
localization_rules: IBM Plex supports an extended Latin, Cyrillic, and Greek range; approved substitute faces cover CJK and other scripts
Layouts are built to mirror cleanly for right-to-left languages
Type sizes are reviewed per script — the Latin scale does not transfer unchanged to CJK

rights_and_licensing.terms: SIL Open Font License 1.1 — no seat limits, no domain restrictions, redistribution permitted with the license
Trademark. Use by non-IBM parties requires written permission; the mark may not be modified under any circumstances.

rights_and_licensing.asset_type: Commissioned photography featuring clients or employees
rights_and_licensing.terms: Usage is bounded by the release signed for each shoot — territory, medium, and duration all vary by asset. Confirm the release before reuse.

permitted: Abstract, textural, and geometric backgrounds consistent with the published visual grammar
Layout exploration and composition variants within the 2x Grid
Diagram and system-illustration drafts in the flat geometric illustration style
prohibited: Generating, redrawing, or approximating the 8-bar mark — it is placed from approved artwork only
Inventing colors outside the published palette, including 'close' variations of IBM Blue
Generating photorealistic people presented as IBM clients, employees, or practitioners
Producing capability claims, product screenshots, or data visualizations with invented figures
Generative type — headlines are set in IBM Plex, never drawn by a model
style_descriptors: restrained, neutral ground with a single deliberate accent
flat geometric construction, consistent stroke weight
natural light, true color, documentary point of view
human_review_required: Any claim, statistic, or capability statement

token_sources.name: Carbon Design System theme and type tokens

source: Built from IBM's public design system materials — the IBM Design Language site, the Carbon Design System documentation and token reference, the IBM Plex repository, and IBM's published accessibility requirements (accessed 2026). Token values are quoted from the public Carbon reference; principles, generation constraints, and rights notes are interpreted from published guidance rather than quoted, and should be confirmed against IBM's internal brand standards before operational use.
